summary: BIOLY is a free browser game that makes learning biology fun. Players visit three planets: they collect leaves in a maze, explore a dark forest with a flashlight to find environmental problems, and replant trees cut down by an AI. Each discovery triggers a biology question from a pool of 35, with a short explanation. We built it because biology is often memorized, not understood. BIOLY turns forest loss, CO₂ and biodiversity into play. Works on phones and computers, in English and Ukrainian.
details:
What it does: BIOLY is a free browser game that teaches biology through space missions about one real problem, the loss of forests. On the Green Planet, players solve a maze and collect leaves; each leaf triggers a biology question, and the exit stays locked until all leaves are found. On the Astro Planet, players sweep a flashlight through a dark forest to uncover pollution, fires and logging, each followed by a question. On the Bioli Planet, an AI cuts trees down and players must replant them against the clock. Questions come from a pool of 35, avoid repeating, and every answer ends with a short explanation.
Benefits: Learning happens through play instead of memorization. Players get instant feedback, earn points, and can replay with new questions every time. It needs no installation or account.
Intended impact: We want students in grades 5-11 to understand how forests, CO2, soil and biodiversity connect, and to care about protecting them. Teachers can use it as a quick classroom activity.
Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, HTML5 Canvas and SVG graphics in a single lightweight file, with browser storage for scores and language. No external libraries. We tested it on phones and computers.
Creativity: Instead of a quiz, biology becomes a story across planets, with a locked exit, a flashlight search and an AI that fights back.
Factors we considered: accessibility (works offline, touch, mouse and keyboard, English and Ukrainian), mobile comfort (the flashlight sits above the finger so it never blocks the view, and mistaken taps are prevented), fair difficulty, and avoiding repeated questions
